Brief item 7: 'Fire's main set is treeroute alone: W and the pair statistics are undefined there, and treeroute's top 3 and own-history share still have values.' compare_shap.py main_text_row() writes treeroute_top3 and own_history_share_treeroute only inside 'if tr and rivals:' (lines 361-386). mismatch_groups.cause: compare_shap.py does not recompute the sign agreement on the draws: no interval, and finite_replicates is written as 0
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Section 8 lists the sign agreement among the 'Pairwise statistics, every pair, both levels' and says 'The importances, every statistic and every number of the main-text row are recomputed per draw. Percentile 95% intervals, each with its number of finite replicates.' Section 10 asks S3.13 for 'pairs x statistics with intervals'. compare_shap.py lines 227-235 evaluate it on the full sample only and write ci_low = ci_high = NaN and finite_replicates = 0, though no draw was evaluated. A and B recompute it on every draw (that draw's top-10 union and signed means, with the determined set fixed by the bootstrap interval, as compare_shap also fixes it) and agree on all 102 pair-levels. Values and signs_compared are equal in all three sources. The 285 keys are 95 pair-levels x (ci_low, ci_high, n_finite). The other 7 pair-levels match: no player is determined in both models on any draw, so A, B and the official file all have null and 0 finite (fire feature: the 4 pairs with treeroute; ndvi: BARDL with treeroute (feature), with LightGBM and with RF (variable)). Fire's variable-level rival_ridge|treeroute is undefined on the full sample but finite on 64 draws: A = B = [0, 1]. No value changes; an interval the protocol's words ask for is missing. Finding for the owner.

mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C15 leaves 'a family with no variable in a problem' open. compare_shap.py lines 268-274 give an empty family a zero row sum and share 0, and coral's main-row own-history shares are 0.00 [0.00, 0.00] with 2,000 finite replicates. B does the same; A writes null with its reason. The keys are 11 family-share interval objects (coral own history x 6 models, defo context and calendar x 5) plus coral's main row: treeroute, median rival, and 3 per-rival entries. The reported numbers are compare_shap's (0). Secondary: the official file also has no interval for these shares (see the family-share group). No B1 problem has an empty family.

mismatch_groups.cause: Feature-level family-share distance (items 1-8): A none, B repeats the variable-level number, compare_shap none
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C15 leaves open 'whether the feature-level pairs carry a family-share distance, and from which phi'. Families are sums of variable-level phi (section 8). compare_shap.py computes tvd_family at the variable level only (lines 281-295), which is A's choice. B repeats the variable-level value (B's X03). The variable-level family distance agrees in all three sources, so no number differs in substance.

mismatch_groups.cause: B1 feature-level family-share distance: A none, B gives a number
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: The same open choice for the pair (main run, B1 run). Section 10: where section 8 is open, the B1 numbers 'make the main comparison's choice (compare_shap.py), as the independent re-computation establishes it'. compare_shap has no feature-level family distance, so A's B1 choice (none) is the one to report. B's value equals its own variable-level B1 family distance, which equals A's (fire 0.8114, pm25 0.7038, ndvi 0.4904). Nothing needs recomputing.

mismatch_groups.cause: Counts have no interval in the official files (n_nonzero, sign_n_determined, sign_n_agree)
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C08 (section 10: 'or whether a count gets an interval'). A and B give the counts intervals and agree. per_lead.json nonzero_players and pairs.parquet signs_compared hold full-sample counts only; the agreeing-sign count is not written but follows from share x count and agrees. compare_shap's choice: no interval for a count. C09 also differs: compare_shap counts nonzero players over J (line 333), A and B over each model's own columns; the counts are equal everywhere. Consequence for B1, by section 10's rule: report the B1 counts (n_nonzero, n_nonzero_before_merge, sign_n_determined, sign_n_agree) without intervals; their values stand.

mismatch_groups.cause: The main row's range (min and max over the rivals) has no interval in the official output
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C22 asks 'whether its ends get intervals'. compare_shap.py lines 379-380 report the full-sample min and max; section 8's row reads 'the median of the top-20-union Spearman [CI] and the range'. A and B add an interval to each end and agree. The min and max values agree in all three sources (coral 0.4148/0.4930, defo 0.0065/0.4685, pm25 -0.1214/0.0793, ndvi -0.4051/0.3841).

mismatch_groups.cause: The official main row names no 'median rival'
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C23. compare_shap takes the numpy median of the rivals' own-history shares (line 385) and names no rival. A and B do the same, and with an odd number of rivals also name the rival whose share is that median: defo and pm25, rival_lgbm. The median's value and interval agree in all three sources (defo 0.3547 [0.3162, 0.3954], pm25 0.2977 [0.2755, 0.3200], ndvi 0.2560 [0.2357, 0.2757]).

mismatch_groups.cause: Item 8: the official files hold only the row counts and the top-10 shares, on the full sample, with shares over every variable
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: Spec C25 leaves open which numbers 'the variable-level importances' are, over which variables the shares are taken, and whether they get intervals. compare_shap.py lines 302-315 report, per arcsine-link model, the rows with pre > 0 and the top 10 [name, share] (per_lead.json nonzero_forecast_rows; the AW3 table). Shares are taken over every variable-level player of the problem. A and B add I, S, intervals, the nonzero count, the ranking and the regions used, with shares over the level's J. The numbers the official files hold equal A's and B's: rows (coral 983, 995, 1,000, 973; fire 226) and every top-10 name, order and share. The two denominators differ only by the structural zeros, which are exactly 0 on those rows. Minor, no effect: compare_shap sorts this top 10 with np.argsort(-Iz), which breaks ties arbitrarily rather than by name; no tie occurred.

mismatch_groups.cause: importance.parquet holds no interval for I, s and S (full-sample values only)
mismatch_groups.diagnosis: A and B give every player's I, share and signed mean (every model, level and problem) a percentile interval with its finite count, and agree on all 21,363 interval objects. compare_shap.py recomputes the importances on every draw (lines 201-208) and uses them for the statistics and the determined signs. It writes only the full-sample mean_abs, share, signed_mean and sign_determined (lines 245-248). Section 8 says the importances are 'recomputed per draw' (they are), but not that each is reported with an interval. Section 10 lists for S3.13 'pairs x statistics with intervals ... each model's top-10 with shares; family shares'. This is not one of the spec's C entries (spec 2.2 item 6: 'The format does not decide which numbers get an interval'). compare_shap's choice: no interval. No reported number changes; A's (= B's) intervals exist if S3.13 wants them. (For B1, section 10 asks for these intervals in so many words.)

mismatch_groups.cause: families.parquet holds no interval for the family shares

A and B give every family share an interval and agree; the full-sample shares agree in all three sources. compare_shap's choice: no interval. No reported number changes.
